basis.governing_question: Which ERP should replace Farmácias Lusas's finance, purchasing and inventory systems, and how is it migrated and rolled out to 40 pharmacies and 2 warehouses?

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Map requirements and process fit for finance, purchasing and inventory across the pharmacies and warehouses.

gate.label: Requirements sign-off
gate.decision: Approve the requirements and go to vendor selection?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Score ERP vendors against the requirements and build the business case for the vendor that fits best.

gate.label: Vendor selection
gate.decision: Which ERP vendor goes forward into implementation?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Configure the ERP, migrate data, and take it live from a pilot site to all pharmacies and warehouses.

gate.label: Final acceptance
gate.decision: Approve the ERP as running in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?

workstreams.name: Finance requirements
workstreams.answers: What must the ERP do for finance at the pharmacies and warehouses?
activities: Interview finance staff and the CFO about today's work
Analyze finance data and documents from the current systems
Write the finance requirements for sign-off

workstreams.name: Purchasing requirements
workstreams.answers: What must the ERP do for purchasing, from ordering to supplier handling, across pharmacies and warehouses?
activities: Interview purchasing staff and pharmacy teams on ordering
Analyze purchasing data and documents from current systems
Write the purchasing requirements for sign-off

workstreams.name: Inventory requirements
workstreams.answers: What must the ERP do for inventory in the pharmacies and both warehouses?
activities: Interview pharmacy and warehouse staff on stock handling
Analyze stock data and documents from current systems
Write the inventory requirements for sign-off

workstreams.name: Process fit-gap
workstreams.answers: Where do today's finance, purchasing and inventory systems fall short of the requirements?
activities: Compare each requirement with how current systems perform
Check gaps in pharmacy and warehouse processes with staff
Consolidate all requirements and gaps for sign-off

workstreams.name: Vendor shortlist and scoring
workstreams.answers: Which ERP vendors fit the signed-off requirements for finance, purchasing and inventory?
activities: Shortlist ERP vendors against the signed-off requirements
Hold ERP demonstrations with pharmacy and warehouse users
Score vendors and check their references with customers

workstreams.name: Business case
workstreams.answers: Does the business case support selecting the ERP vendor that fits the requirements best?
activities: Estimate costs and benefits for the vendors in contention
Test the case with the CFO and the Operations Director
Assemble the evidence for the vendor selection decision

workstreams.name: Configuration and testing
workstreams.answers: Can the ERP be configured and tested for finance, purchasing and inventory in the pharmacies and both warehouses?
activities: Configure finance and purchasing to the requirements
Configure inventory for pharmacies and warehouses
Test each area with the people who run it and fix defects

workstreams.name: Data migration
workstreams.answers: Can the data from today's systems be migrated into the ERP and checked as complete?
activities: Map and clean data from today's systems for loading
Rehearse the data load and reconcile it with source records
Report rehearsal results for the readiness review

workstreams.name: Pilot site go-live
workstreams.answers: Does the ERP run live and stable at a pilot site for finance, purchasing and inventory?
activities: Prepare the pilot site and train its staff for go-live
Run the pilot site live and track stability and issues
Report pilot results for review at the workshop

workstreams.name: Site rollout in waves
workstreams.answers: Can the ERP go live wave by wave in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?
activities: Train staff and prepare the sites in each wave
Take each wave of pharmacies and warehouses live
Track use in each live site against the success criterion

deliverables.name: Fit-gap findings for finance and purchasing
Consolidated requirements and fit-gap for sign-off
Vendor scoring and customer reference checks
Business case and vendor scoring for selection decision
Configured finance and purchasing with test results
Tested ERP configuration for all process areas
Data migration rehearsal and reconciliation results
Final acceptance pack for all pharmacies and warehouses

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Agree the access the diagnostic needs
events.decision: Confirm access to finance, purchasing and inventory data and process owners?
agenda: Present the engagement objective, phases and gates
Review the data and process owners the diagnostic needs
Confirm who gives access to each from week 1

events.label: Check-in: requirements
events.decision: Which fit-gap findings need more detail before requirements sign-off?
agenda: Present the finance, purchasing and inventory requirements
Review the fit-gap findings for finance and purchasing
Discuss which findings need more detail before sign-off

events.label: Requirements sign-off
events.decision: Approve the requirements and go to vendor selection?
agenda: Present the consolidated requirements and fit-gap
Review open gaps by process area
Decide whether to move to vendor selection

events.label: Check-in: vendor scoring
events.decision: Which scored vendors go into the final comparison at the selection gate?
agenda: Present the vendor shortlist and scoring
Review the customer reference check results
Discuss which vendors enter the final comparison

events.label: Vendor selection
events.purpose: Select the vendor to take forward
events.decision: Which ERP vendor goes forward into implementation?
agenda: Present the business case and vendor scoring
Review reference checks and the shortlist
Decide which vendor goes into implementation

events.label: Check-in: test results
events.purpose: Review finance and purchasing test results
events.decision: Which open test issues in finance and purchasing must close before data migration?
agenda: Present configured finance and purchasing with test results
Review open test issues by process area
Discuss which issues must close before migration

events.label: Workshop 1: pilot readiness
events.decision: Go or no-go on starting the pilot site go-live given readiness results?
agenda: Present the tested configuration and migration reconciliation
Review open issues that could affect go-live
Decide whether the pilot site goes live

events.label: Workshop 2: pilot results
events.decision: Start the first rollout wave, or extend the pilot to close open issues?
agenda: Present the pilot go-live record and stability report
Review open pilot issues and their effect on rollout
Decide whether to start the first wave or extend the pilot

events.label: Check-in: rollout wave 1
events.decision: What must change in the remaining waves to reach acceptance in all sites?
agenda: Present the first rollout wave go-live record
Review wave 1 results against the acceptance criterion
Discuss what the remaining waves need to reach all sites

events.label: Final acceptance
events.purpose: Accept the ERP across all sites
events.decision: Approve the ERP as running in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?
agenda: Present the final acceptance pack
Review go-live results across all pharmacies and warehouses
Decide whether to approve the ERP as running in all sites

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given, so every duration is an estimate to confirm before quoting.
Implementation takes the middle of a 23 to 34 week estimate; it reaches the top if areas take 6 weeks and waves 3 weeks.
Implementation is added to the technology selection archetype's Diagnostic and Design because the brief includes data migration and rollout to 40 pharmacies and 2 warehouses.
Design assumes shortlist and demonstrations without a formal tender; a tender would add 4 to 6 weeks and should be confirmed.

sub_questions.question: What must the ERP do for finance, purchasing and inventory, and where do today's systems fall short?
Which ERP fits the requirements, and does its business case support selecting it?
Can the ERP be configured, tested and loaded with migrated data for finance, purchasing and inventory?
Can the ERP run live and stable at a pilot site, then in all 40 pharmacies and both warehouses?

drivers.evidence: roll it out to its 40 pharmacies and 2 warehouses

phases.name: Diagnostic

work.unit: Process area mapped with its requirements

phases.why: Three process areas mapped two at a time, plus start-up and synthesis weeks; inside the archetype's typical 3 to 6 weeks.

phases.name: Design
phases.why: One shortlist, demonstration and scoring round, then a synthesis week; no formal tender assumed. Inside the archetype's typical 4 to 8 weeks.

phases.name: Implementation

work.unit: System configured and tested for one process area
Rollout wave of up to 10 sites

phases.why: Areas configured two at a time, then one migration rehearsal, one pilot site and five rollout waves of up to 10 sites, in sequence.

sizing.levers: Rollout waves two at a time would save 4 to 6 weeks; configuring all three process areas together would save 4 to 6 more.
